title: Typed reversible route map
description: A reversible route factory, canonical safe-integer codec, and ordered route-map matcher.
whenToUse: Use when application code must build and match the same typed URLs without losing default, optional, or repeated search semantics.

title: Backpressured asynchronous operation
description: A bounded-capacity normalizer plus operation producer and concurrent drain helpers.
whenToUse: Use when one owner needs ordered progress values, a terminal result, cooperative cancellation, and bounded producer run-ahead.

title: Typed JSON HTTP contract and router
description: A small Standard Schema adapter, typed router declaration, JSON contract, and native Fetch handler scaffold.
whenToUse: Use when trusted server code must validate a JSON API while browser consumers retain status-discriminated types and typed route inputs.

title: Validated reactive collection
description: Dense finite-number validation, atomic SignalArray replacement, computed projection, and effect observation.
whenToUse: Use when native-shaped collection mutations should update derived state without allowing sparse or non-finite inputs through an adapter boundary.

title: Owned local message session
description: A complete MessageChannel request, subscription, cancellation, transfer, and ownership scaffold.
whenToUse: Use when one component owns both ends of a typed worker-style protocol and must close protocol resources separately from transport resources.

title: Node Uint8Array base64 encoding
description: Strict option normalization and Node-only encoding helpers that preserve Uint8Array view boundaries.
whenToUse: Use when Node code needs the Uint8Array toBase64 contract without modifying globals.

title: Nested asynchronous resource scope
description: A package-symbol resource scope that preserves acquisition or work errors beneath every later cleanup failure.
whenToUse: Use when mixed synchronous and asynchronous resources need LIFO cleanup and an exact SuppressedError tree.

title: Dormant gated signal effect
description: A dormant effect controller with synchronous initial publication, microtask scheduling, an explicit disabled branch, and idempotent disposal.
whenToUse: Use when cleanup must be registered before an effect starts or when enabled and disabled states both need observable publication.
